overview: Sempra is a San Diego-based holding company whose principal businesses are regulated electric and natural gas utilities in California (SDG&E, SoCalGas) and Texas (an 80.25% equity-method stake in Oncor, the largest T&D utility in ERCOT, plus a 50% stake in Sharyland Utilities), together with Sempra Infrastructure, which develops and operates LNG export, pipeline/energy-network and low-carbon infrastructure in the U.S. and Mexico (Cameron LNG, Port Arthur LNG, ECA LNG, Mexican pipelines). Sempra is mid-way through a 'capital recycling' program -- selling 45% of Sempra Infrastructure Partners (SI Partners) to a KKR-led consortium for ~$9.99 billion and its Mexican gas utility Ecogas for ~$500 million -- to fund a record five-year, ~$65 billion capital plan that is now over 95% weighted toward its regulated California and Texas utilities.

business_model.summary: Cost-of-service regulated utility earnings at SDG&E, SoCalGas and (via equity method) Oncor, supplemented by contracted, fee-based LNG export and pipeline cash flows at Sempra Infrastructure under long-term (15-30 year) take-or-pay offtake agreements with investment-grade counterparties (TotalEnergies, ConocoPhillips, Mitsubishi, Mitsui, RWE, INEOS, Orlen, ENGIE, EQT, JERA), plus a smaller natural gas/LNG asset-optimization trading business. Natural gas commodity costs are passed through to utility customers without markup.

revenue_streams.name: Natural gas utility revenue (Sempra California + Sempra Infrastructure/Ecogas)
Sempra Infrastructure energy-related businesses (LNG, pipelines, LPG, power)

business_model.customer_type: Regulated monopoly B2C/B2B ratepayers (residential, commercial, industrial) in San Diego/Southern California and Texas, plus B2B long-term contracted LNG/pipeline customers (global utilities, oil majors, traders)
business_model.geographic_mix: California (SDG&E + SoCalGas service territories covering ~21+ million people) and Texas (Oncor serves >4.1 million delivery points across ERCOT) generate the vast majority of segment earnings; Sempra Infrastructure's LNG and pipeline assets are in the U.S. Gulf Coast (Louisiana, Texas) and Mexico (Baja California, Sonora)

main_competitors: Southern California Edison / PG&E (CA utility peers)
Cheniere Energy / NextDecade / Venture Global (U.S. LNG export)
Other Mexican energy infrastructure developers (CFE, PEMEX-adjacent)
competitive_position.market_position: Sole franchised electric/gas distributor in its San Diego and Southern/Central California service territories; Oncor is the largest electric T&D utility in Texas by customers and circuit miles; Sempra Infrastructure is a top-tier North American LNG developer (Cameron, Port Arthur, ECA) with multiple projects under construction

moat_factors.description: SDG&E, SoCalGas and Oncor hold exclusive certificated service territories with CPUC/PUCT-approved cost-of-service rate recovery
Port Arthur, Cameron and ECA LNG trains are substantially pre-sold under 15-30 year SPAs with investment-grade counterparties, reducing volume/price risk once operational
Decades-old transmission, distribution and pipeline networks are not economically duplicable
Oncor's incumbent position captures outsized share of ERCOT's data-center/AI-driven load growth (33.3 GW peak, ~24 GW of Batch Zero large load)
Decades of CPUC/PUCT/FERC regulatory history, though increasingly adversarial in California

weaknesses: No operating control over Oncor (ring-fenced, equity-method 80.25% stake) or, after the KKR transaction, over SI Partners (reduced to a 25% minority interest)
California wildfire liability under the strict-liability inverse condemnation doctrine, with imperfect and sometimes denied cost recovery
Recurring CPUC regulatory lag and disallowances (e.g., $651 million 2024 GRC Track 2 wildfire-mitigation disallowance)
Heavy reliance on continuous debt and equity (ATM) issuance to fund a capital-intensive, multi-decade growth plan
Mexico/Sempra Infrastructure exposure to foreign currency, nationalization and an increasingly state-controlled energy policy

growth_drivers: Record five-year (2026-2030) capital plan of ~$65 billion (up from $56 billion in the prior plan), with over 95% directed to regulated California and Texas utility rate base, targeting an 11% rate base CAGR

Oncor/ERCOT data-center and AI-driven load growth -- 33.3 GW system peak (+6%), ~24 GW of large load reclassified as 'Batch Zero' base load, and a 2027-2031 capital plan expected to rise ~20% above the prior $47.5 billion plan
Texas Unified Transmission and Distribution Mechanism (UTM, enacted June 2025) and surcharge/rate-review mechanisms that reduce regulatory lag on Oncor's capital investment
Capital recycling: ~$9.99 billion SI Partners stake sale to KKR/ADIA and ~$500 million Ecogas sale fund the utility capital plan while deleveraging and simplifying Sempra's Mexico/LNG risk exposure

LNG buildout: Port Arthur LNG Phase 1 (COD ~2027-2028) and Phase 2 (FID reached Sept 2025, COD ~2030-2031), plus ECA LNG Phase 1 nearing commercial operations in 2026, adding substantially contracted LNG export capacity
Long-term EPS growth target of 7%-9% and a 2030 adjusted EPS outlook of $6.70-$7.50

business.description: SoCalGas/SDG&E remain defendants in Palisades and Eaton fire (LA Fires, Jan 2025) litigation, and a new Norte Fire lawsuit was filed against SDG&E/Sempra in October 2026; inverse condemnation imposes strict liability regardless of fault

business.risk: Loss of control over key assets
business.description: Ring-fencing limits influence over Oncor; the pending/closing KKR transaction cuts Sempra's SI Partners stake to 25%, ceding control of LNG/Mexico assets to KKR

A fatal construction incident at Port Arthur LNG I (April 2025, 3 deaths) and greenfield-site cost/schedule risk illustrate large-project execution exposure across Port Arthur, ECA and Cameron Phase 2
Mexico's 2024 constitutional reforms and 2025 Energy Laws increase state control (CFE/PEMEX) over the energy sector, pressuring IEnova-related permits, tariffs and self-supply projects

financial.description: Moody's (Baa2) and S&P (BBB+) carry negative outlooks on Sempra, partly citing wildfire risk; any downgrade raises borrowing costs and could trigger Oncor dividend restrictions
A ~$65 billion five-year capex plan requires ongoing debt issuance and ATM equity sales (up to $3.0 billion program), creating dilution and refinancing risk in a higher-rate environment
Unhedged net investment in Mexican-peso-denominated Sempra Infrastructure operations creates OCI volatility and monetary-position gains/losses

regulatory.description: The 2024 GRC Track 2 final decision disallowed $651 million of wildfire-mitigation costs; a pending CPUC proposed decision could deny correction of a 2024 GRC attrition mechanism (~$188 million), pushing 2027 EPS toward the low end of guidance
SDG&E's TO5/TO6 transmission ROE and California ISO adder have been litigated with FERC since 2024; a June 2026 settlement resolved TO6 but outcomes remain subject to further proceedings

regulatory.risk: PUCT/ERCOT rate case and interconnection risk
regulatory.description: Oncor's comprehensive base rate reviews, UTM implementation and large-load (data center) interconnection rules are still being finalized by the PUCT and could change economics of planned capex

macro.description: As a highly capital-intensive, debt-funded utility holding company, Sempra's financing costs and equity cost of capital are sensitive to interest-rate moves, partially offset by California's cost-of-capital mechanism (CCM)
Rising California and Texas customer rates from large capital programs increase political and regulatory pushback risk, potentially slowing cost recovery

Natural gas costs are largely pass-through for utility customers, but Sempra Infrastructure's asset-optimization and un-hedged derivative positions create earnings volatility from gas/power price swings

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. regulated utilities are benefiting from a multi-year capital upcycle driven by grid modernization, electrification and, especially in ERCOT/Texas, data-center and AI-driven load growth; U.S. LNG exports continue to expand as a structural beneficiary of global gas demand and energy-security policy, though competing with Qatari and other North American supply
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low for the California and Texas regulated-utility segments (defensive, rate-base-driven earnings); moderate-to-high for Sempra Infrastructure's LNG/commodity-optimization business, which is exposed to global gas prices, FX and project-completion timing
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High -- Sempra funds a ~$65 billion five-year capex plan primarily with debt and ATM equity issuance; CPUC's cost-of-capital mechanism (CCM) and FERC/PUCT formula rates provide partial, lagged offsets
key_input_costs: Steel, transformers and other grid/pipeline construction materials (tariff-exposed)
Skilled construction/EPC labor (Bechtel and other contractors)

recent_developments.event: LA Fires (Palisades and Eaton) burned in SoCalGas' service territory; SoCalGas and Sempra named as defendants in consolidated litigation; Sempra was later dismissed from the Palisades action (July 2026) but SoCalGas remains a defendant
Fatal construction incident at the Port Arthur LNG I project (3 Bechtel employee deaths); related lawsuits settled in principle by August 2026, with Bechtel indemnifying under its EPC contract

Agreed to sell a 45% equity interest in SI Partners to a KKR-led consortium (with ADIA retaining 10%) for ~$9.99 billion; reached positive FID and sold a 49.9% stake in Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 to Blackstone-led investors
The 2025 California Wildfire Legislation was signed, establishing an $18 billion Continuation Account to supplement the existing Wildfire Fund
SDG&E recorded a $651 million ($464M after-tax) charge from the CPUC's 2024 GRC Track 2 final decision disallowing certain wildfire-mitigation cost recovery; agreed to sell Ecogas for ~$500 million
SoCalGas' CODM/president role moved to an interim basis
Oncor implemented new base rates under a comprehensive base rate review settlement (9.75% ROE / 43.5% equity layer); FERC approved SDG&E's TO6 transmission rate settlement
Completed the sale of Ecogas, recognizing a pretax gain (~$97-198 million depending on FX hedge treatment); SI Partners sale to KKR consortium rescheduled to close November 2026
A new wildfire (the 'Norte Fire') near San Clemente, California prompted a lawsuit against SDG&E, Enova and Sempra alleging its equipment caused the fire; cause remains under investigation

Reported Q3 2026 results: adjusted EPS of $1.40 beat consensus (~$1.20) on Texas Utilities strength; raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to the high end of $4.80-$5.30 and GAAP guidance to $7.41-$8.41, while flagging a pending CPUC proposed decision that could push 2027 EPS toward the low end of the $5.10-$5.70 range

First full-year 2030 outlook, issued alongside the expanded five-year capital plan
Underpinned by rate base growth and the capital-recycling program
Reflects the expanded $65 billion five-year capital plan

Excludes the Eastern 765-kV Strategic Transmission Expansion Plan, SRP and Batch Zero large-load capex, which represent further upside

guidance.management_commentary: Management described the Texas/Oncor data-center and large-load growth pipeline (33.3 GW system peak, ~24 GW of Batch Zero base load) as the primary upside driver, while characterizing the California CPUC proposed decision risk as a 2027-specific issue it would seek to mitigate; it also noted Texas O&M inflation running 1-1.5 points above the national average and called post-election Texas regulatory/political dynamics 'too early to tell.'

bull_case: An 11% rate base CAGR and 7%-9% long-term EPS growth are underpinned by a record ~$65 billion five-year capital plan, over 95% of which flows into constructively regulated California and Texas utility rate base

Oncor/ERCOT offers one of the strongest grid growth stories in the U.S. given AI/data-center load growth (33.3 GW peak, ~24 GW of newly classified base load), with Oncor's own capital plan already guided ~20% higher

Capital recycling (the ~$9.99 billion SI Partners stake sale to KKR/ADIA and the Ecogas sale) funds the utility growth plan while deleveraging the balance sheet and reducing Mexico/LNG risk concentration

Substantially pre-contracted LNG capacity (20-30 year SPAs with investment-grade counterparties across Port Arthur, Cameron and ECA) should convert to largely de-risked, long-duration cash flows as projects reach commercial operation through 2031
Q3 2026 results beat expectations and management raised 2026 guidance to the high end of its range, signaling positive earnings momentum heading into 2027
bear_case: California wildfire liability is an open-ended tail risk: ongoing Palisades/Eaton fire litigation against SoCalGas and a newly filed (October 2026) Norte Fire lawsuit against SDG&E/Sempra sit under the strict-liability inverse condemnation doctrine with imperfect insurance and rate recovery

CPUC regulatory lag and disallowances are a recurring earnings drag -- the $651 million 2024 GRC Track 2 charge and a pending proposed decision could push 2027 EPS to the low end of guidance, illustrating California's increasingly adversarial regulatory environment

Credit ratings carry negative outlooks at Moody's and S&P, and the expanded $65 billion capex plan requires sustained debt and dilutive ATM equity issuance in a still-elevated interest-rate environment

Sempra lacks operating control over its two largest growth assets -- Oncor (ring-fenced equity-method stake) and, pending the KKR transaction's close, SI Partners (reduced to a 25% minority interest) -- ceding governance and distribution terms to outside partners

LNG/Mexico infrastructure carries real execution risk, evidenced by the fatal Port Arthur LNG I construction incident and Mexico's increasingly nationalist 2025 Energy Laws, which could pressure returns on IEnova-related permits and self-supply projects
